groups.sound: S / SH / CH — hissing and hushing sounds
groups.note: S: tongue tip just behind the teeth, lips relaxed, a thin sharp stream of air. SH: lips rounded and pushed forward, tongue pulled slightly back — a wider, softer stream. CH is SH with a quick T in front. Keep each sound crisp and never let S and SH blur into each other.

groups.sound: TH — the tongue between the teeth
groups.note: Place the tip of the tongue lightly between the upper and lower teeth and let air pass over it. In “think” and “three” it is voiceless (just air); in “this” and “that” the voice is on. Don't replace TH with S, F, T or D.

groups.sound: R / L — the tongue lifts and curls
groups.note: L: the tongue tip presses on the ridge behind the upper teeth and air flows around its sides. English R: the tongue tip does not touch anything — it curls slightly back, the lips round a little. Switch between them cleanly without slurring.

groups.note: Close the lips firmly. P is a puff of air with no voice; B is the same closure with the voice on; M keeps the lips closed and hums through the nose. Let the lips work actively — no lazy, half-closed mouth.

groups.note: The tongue tip taps the ridge just behind the upper teeth and releases quickly. T is voiceless with a small puff of air; D is the same tap with the voice on. Keep the taps light and precise, especially at the ends of words.

groups.note: The back of the tongue rises to the soft palate, blocks the air and releases it sharply. K is voiceless with a puff of air; G is the same with the voice on. Keep the jaw relaxed and the release clean.

groups.sound: W / V / F — lips and teeth
groups.note: W: round the lips into a small circle, then open them quickly — the teeth don't touch the lip. V and F: the upper teeth rest lightly on the lower lip; F is just air, V adds the voice. Don't swap W and V.

groups.sound: Vowels, Y and H — open, clear sounds
groups.note: Open the mouth fully and give every vowel its own clear shape — round the lips for “oo” and “ow”, spread them for “ee”. Y glides into the vowel; H is a gentle breath, never swallowed. Don't let unstressed vowels turn into mumbling.
